l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time flight progress network-wide
l4_steps.input: Live ACARS position reports, gate departure/arrival feeds
l4_steps.output: Real-time operational picture displayed on NOC wall board
l4_steps.kpi: Flight tracking refresh rate ≤60 sec; network visibility ≥99.5% uptime
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS datalink gaps over oceanic/remote sectors create blind spots; controller must cross-reference multiple screens to build situational awareness

l4_steps.name: Ingest weather and ATC flow constraint data
l4_steps.input: METARs, TAFs, SIGMETs, FAA TFMS/SWIM Ground Delay Programs
l4_steps.output: Weather impact overlay on network map; GDP-affected flight list
l4_steps.kpi: Weather advisory ingestion latency ≤5 min from SIGMET issue
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA TFMS GDP notifications arrive via multiple channels (NAS Status, SWIM API, phone) with no single consolidated feed — manual reconciliation required

l4_steps.name: Assess airport capacity and slot utilisation
l4_steps.input: Airport slot allocations, gate availability, ground handler capacity
l4_steps.output: Slot utilisation report; gate conflict alerts
l4_steps.kpi: Gate conflict identification ≥30 min before scheduled pushback
l4_steps.pain_point: At slot-controlled airports (LHR, JFK), late slot returns trigger IATA WASG 80:20 use-it-or-lose-it penalties — NOC must balance recovery options against slot forfeiture risk

l4_steps.name: Detect operational deviation and trigger disruption alert
l4_steps.input: Automated threshold breach: delay >15 min, ATC hold, maintenance release flag
l4_steps.output: Disruption alert ticket with affected flight list and estimated downstream cascade
l4_steps.kpi: Alert-to-triage response time ≤10 min for Severity 1 events
l4_steps.pain_point: Cairo AI cascade modelling accuracy degrades when multiple simultaneous disruptions interact — controller must validate AI-generated impact scores manually for compounding events

l4_steps.name: Classify disruption severity and operational scope
l4_steps.input: Disruption alert ticket; affected flight count; estimated delay propagation
l4_steps.output: Severity classification (S1 Network Crisis / S2 Station Event / S3 Single Flight)
l4_steps.kpi: Correct severity classification rate ≥95% vs post-event review
l4_steps.pain_point: No standardised severity matrix shared between NOC, Crew Scheduling, and Maintenance Control — classification disagreements delay activation of the correct recovery protocol

l4_steps.name: Model downstream cascade impact on network
l4_steps.input: Disruption origin flight; rotational aircraft tail assignments; crew pairings
l4_steps.output: Cascade impact map: N flights affected, estimated total delay minutes, PAX count at risk
l4_steps.kpi: Cascade model produced within 5 min of S1/S2 alert; PAX-at-risk count accuracy ±5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Aircraft tail swap history held in Jeppesen Crew and SITA AMS separately — reconciling rotational conflicts across systems requires manual data export and is error-prone at speed

l4_steps.name: Escalate network-wide crisis to senior NOC leadership
l4_steps.input: S1 severity classification; cascade impact map
l4_steps.output: Crisis bridge call initiated; senior leadership (VP Operations, VP Maintenance) notified; war room convened
l4_steps.kpi: Senior leadership notified within 15 min of S1 classification
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline-specific: post-Dec 2022 IROPS crisis, several carriers lack documented escalation runbooks — NOC managers default to ad hoc phone calls, creating coordination gaps during high-stress events

l4_steps.name: Identify available spare aircraft for recovery
l4_steps.input: Current fleet status board; maintenance release schedule; spare aircraft positions
l4_steps.output: Candidate spare aircraft list with position, range capability, and availability window
l4_steps.kpi: Spare aircraft identified within 20 min of disruption classification for S1/S2 events
l4_steps.pain_point: Unscheduled AOG maintenance removes spare aircraft without real-time update to NOC fleet board — controllers discover unavailability only when attempting to assign tail, causing recovery plan rework

l4_steps.name: Model and score recovery scenario options
l4_steps.input: Spare aircraft list; delay propagation model; crew availability matrix
l4_steps.output: Ranked recovery scenarios with cost, delay, and PAX-impact scores
l4_steps.kpi: ≥3 recovery scenarios generated per S1/S2 event; scenario scoring completed within 10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Cairo AI optimisation is constrained by static crew legality rules embedded at implementation — dynamic FAR Part 117 duty time calculations for mixed international/domestic pairings require manual override by Crew Scheduling

l4_steps.name: Evaluate crew duty legality for recovery assignments
l4_steps.input: Proposed recovery flight assignments; crew current duty start times and rest records
l4_steps.output: Legal/illegal flag per crew pairing; compliant alternatives where required
l4_steps.kpi: Zero FAR Part 117 duty-time violations in executed recovery plan; crew legality check completed within 15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen legality engine checks planned duties but cannot pre-validate real-time operator-initiated tail swaps — illegal assignments may only surface at sign-in, causing last-minute scrambles

l4_steps.name: Select and approve final recovery plan
l4_steps.input: Scored recovery scenarios; crew legality validation; cost approval authority
l4_steps.output: Approved recovery plan with assigned tail numbers, crew, and revised schedule
l4_steps.kpi: Recovery plan approved and published within 30 min of S1 disruption onset
l4_steps.pain_point: Financial authority thresholds for ferry flights and hotel costs are not pre-delegated to NOC duty managers — approvals requiring VP sign-off during off-peak hours introduce 30–60 min delays

l4_steps.name: Issue crew reassignment instructions to Crew Scheduling
l4_steps.input: Approved recovery plan; reserve crew roster; current crew positions
l4_steps.output: Crew reassignment notifications sent via CrewTrac; updated pairing records
l4_steps.kpi: Crew contact-and-confirm cycle completed within 20 min; reserve activation rate ≥90% first contact
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew contactability drops during off-hours — contactability SLA is not contractually mandated beyond 2-hour reserve callout window, limiting rapid IROPS response capability

l4_steps.name: Coordinate aircraft maintenance release with MCC
l4_steps.input: Recovery aircraft tail number; open deferred defects (DD) list; MEL status
l4_steps.output: Maintenance release confirmation or deferred defect deferral decision
l4_steps.kpi: Aircraft release decision issued within 30 min of MCC request for non-AOG aircraft
l4_steps.pain_point: MEL deferral decisions on borderline items require OEM (Boeing) consultation — Boeing's 24/7 technical operations line response time can reach 60+ min for complex MEL calls, blocking aircraft release

l4_steps.name: Issue gate changes and ground resource reallocation
l4_steps.input: Revised aircraft routing; gate availability; ground handler and fuelling schedules
l4_steps.output: Gate reassignment notices; revised ground service orders to handlers
l4_steps.kpi: Ground resources confirmed at revised gate ≥45 min before revised departure
l4_steps.pain_point: At contracted-handler airports, gate change notifications must be transmitted via SITA messaging — handlers operating legacy systems acknowledge with 15–30 min lag, preventing NOC from confirming readiness

l4_steps.name: Update revised schedule and flight status in Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Approved recovery plan; revised departure times; aircraft and crew assignments
l4_steps.output: Updated flight records in Altéa DCS; GDS flight status broadcast via SITA Type B messages
l4_steps.kpi: Schedule update published to GDS within 10 min of plan approval; zero discrepancies between Altéa and SITA AMS flight status
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual rescheduling in Altéa for >10 flights simultaneously requires sequential data entry — bulk SSIM import is available but requires IT ops involvement, creating a bottleneck during mass IROPS events

l4_steps.name: Trigger automated passenger rebooking workflow
l4_steps.input: Cancelled/significantly delayed flights; passenger itinerary records; rebooking rules policy
l4_steps.output: Automated rebooking confirmations sent to affected PAX via email/SMS; waitlist cleared
l4_steps.kpi: ≥85% of disrupted PAX rebooked within 2 hours of cancellation; EU261/DOT delay notification compliance 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa automated rebooking applies FIFO logic that ignores high-value loyalty tier passengers — premium PAX may be rebooked on worse itineraries than low-tier PAX unless NDC/API rules override is manually triggered

l4_steps.name: Monitor recovery execution and track plan adherence
l4_steps.input: Real-time departure/arrival feeds; crew sign-in confirmations; maintenance release updates
l4_steps.output: Recovery tracking dashboard; variance alerts when execution deviates >15 min from plan
l4_steps.kpi: Recovery plan adherence ≥80% of revised departure times met within ±15 min; total network delay minutes reduced ≥40% vs no-action baseline
l4_steps.pain_point: No unified real-time recovery adherence score exists — NOC manager must manually correlate Altéa flight status, Jeppesen crew sign-ins, and SITA AMS gate data to determine if recovery is on track

l4_steps.name: Document NOC event log and decision audit trail
l4_steps.input: Chronological decision log; communications record; final recovery outcomes
l4_steps.output: Closed NOC event ticket with full audit trail; regulatory documentation for DOT/CAA if required
l4_steps.kpi: Event documentation completed within 4 hours of network recovery; 100% of S1 events produce a formal After-Action Report
l4_steps.pain_point: Decision rationale during fast-moving IROPS is rarely captured in real time — post-event reconstruction from chat logs and ACARS data is time-consuming and incomplete, undermining root cause analysis
